children: is preparing a diesel-hybrid option for its future generation of large vans, with development work assigned to its Pratola Serra engine facility in southern Italy.

The project links the engine plant with the automaker’s vehicle manufacturing site in Atessa, where the next generation of vans is expected to offer the new powertrain. Italy’s Uilm union outlined the plan following a meeting with Stellantis
The technology remains under evaluation, and no launch date has been set, a company spokesperson said. Stellantis
has announced an investment of €1 billion ($1.12 billion) for the Atessa project.
The automaker sells its large vans under the Fiat Ducato, Peugeot Boxer and Citroën Jumper nameplates.
Separately, the Uilm union said furloughs at Stellantis
plants in Italy are expected to decline by 30% in 2026 compared with the previous year.
Shares of the automaker were trading about 2% higher on Thursday.

title: Stellantis explores diesel hybrid powertrain for future van models
